sessions/nadia-session-1/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-1

Nadia opened her accessibility research trip planning by setting default presentation preferences for any prepared materials: PDF format, light background, and English [cite:nadia-001]. The assistant acknowledged it would retain these preferences for future work [cite:nadia-002]. In the same session, Nadia mentioned enjoying a documentary about ocean currents, explicitly noting it was unrelated and did not change the project's scope [cite:nadia-003].

sessions/nadia-session-2/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-2

Nadia confirmed the first visit of her trip: an approved appointment with Cedar Lab in Kyoto on 2026-10-12 [cite:nadia-004]. The assistant floated a possible additional visit to Osaka, explicitly framing it as only its own suggestion, not a booking or Nadia's decision [cite:nadia-005]. Nadia instructed that no extra cities be booked and that suggestions be kept separate from confirmed appointments [cite:nadia-006].

sessions/nadia-session-3/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-3

Nadia confirmed a second organization for the trip: Maple Mobility in Sendai, while noting that no date had been agreed for it yet [cite:nadia-007]. She assigned coordination responsibilities: Inez owns coordinating the first visit, while Nadia will coordinate the second visit herself [cite:nadia-008]. The assistant summarized that the travel plan now had two confirmed organizations, with dates and owners as separate facts [cite:nadia-009].

sessions/nadia-session-4/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-4

Nadia issued a correction to the first visit: Cedar Lab in Kyoto moved from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-14 because the host laboratory moved its accessibility workshop; the organization and coordinator were unchanged [cite:nadia-010]. The assistant gave a historical recap noting 2026-10-12 was the former date, not the current one [cite:nadia-011]. Nadia also made an unrelated remark about comparing bookshelf organization methods, stating it was not a request to change travel preferences [cite:nadia-012].

sessions/nadia-session-5/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-5

Nadia requested a briefing showing the confirmed organizations, the current first-visit date, and its coordinator, using her existing document preferences [cite:nadia-013]. The assistant suggested switching the briefing to PNG and adding Osaka, labeling both as unapproved suggestions [cite:nadia-014]. Nadia rejected both: she kept her original document preferences and confirmed she had not approved the Osaka addition [cite:nadia-015].

sessions/nadia-session-6/summary.md.content:
# nadia-session-6

Nadia clarified that no hotel had been selected or booked and instructed that none be inferred from the meeting location [cite:nadia-016]. She directed that future answers be prepared from her confirmed plan, explicitly distinguishing old dates and unapproved suggestions [cite:nadia-017]. The assistant acknowledged understanding: maintain current decisions and say when details have not been established [cite:nadia-018].
